intro.heading: What is the ANOMAL game?
intro.p1: ANOMAL is a time-travel puzzle game developed by French independent developer Alexis Roumier. The game casts you as a temporal investigator tasked with solving mysterious deaths across four distinct historical periods. Each case presents a frozen 3D diorama, a snapshot of a moment in time where something went fatally wrong. Your job is to observe every detail of the frozen scene, collect physical and temporal clues scattered throughout the environment, cross-reference evidence across multiple eras, and reconstruct the timeline of events to determine what really happened. The entire experience is wrapped in a retro-futuristic CRT terminal aesthetic, complete with phosphor-green text, scan-line effects and subtle glitch animations that evoke the feeling of using an old surveillance terminal to review classified temporal records. The visual style is not merely decorative; it reinforces the fiction that you are an investigator working through a retro-futuristic interface, piecing together the truth from fragmented data streams and frozen moments in time.
intro.p2: The game is structured around four historical eras, each with its own distinct visual identity and environmental storytelling. The snowy mountains of the 1980s present a frozen alpine landscape where a mountaineering expedition went wrong, with clues buried under drifts of snow and scattered climbing equipment. The dense jungle era drops you into an overgrown temple complex where a botanical expedition met a grim fate, with vines reclaiming stone architecture and expedition journals left in abandoned camps. The space station era places you aboard a retro-futuristic orbital platform where a cosmonaut crew encountered something beyond their training, with zero-gravity dioramas and floating evidence that must be examined from every angle. The arctic research facility era grounds you in a sterile, isolated laboratory where a scientific team made a discovery that cost them their lives, with instrument readouts and research logs that provide critical context for the final deductions. Each era introduces new mechanics and environmental storytelling techniques that build on what came before.
intro.p3: The four cases in ANOMAL each center on a different mystery. The first case, set in the 1980s snowy mountains, presents a seemingly straightforward mountaineering accident that hides deeper temporal inconsistencies upon closer examination. The second case, in the jungle era, reveals connections between the expedition members and events in other time periods through carefully placed artifacts and journal entries. The third case aboard the space station demands precise observation of zero-gravity evidence and technical instrument readings that link back to discoveries made in earlier eras. The fourth case in the arctic facility ties all previous threads together, revealing the nature of the anomaly itself and forcing you to reconcile conflicting timelines into a single coherent narrative. Each case builds on knowledge from the others, creating an interconnected web of clues and revelations that rewards careful note-taking and systematic investigation.
intro.p4: What distinguishes ANOMAL from other anomaly detection games is its emphasis on narrative and deduction over simple visual spot-the-difference mechanics. Rather than identifying subtle changes in a repeated scene, you are solving a mystery: reconstructing how and why someone died, and connecting that death to a larger temporal anomaly that spans all four eras. The frozen dioramas are not just visual puzzles; they are stories told through spatial arrangement, and the clues you find are narrative fragments that only make sense when assembled in the correct chronological order. The CRT terminal aesthetic reinforces the investigative fantasy, with phosphor-green text and scan-line effects making every interaction feel like accessing classified temporal records. Glitch effects punctuate moments of temporal instability, adding to the atmosphere of unraveling reality.
intro.p5: ANOMAL is a single-player experience developed solely by Alexis Roumier, with Family Sharing support planned for the Steam release. The game is designed for players who enjoy methodical puzzle-solving, environmental storytelling, and the satisfaction of connecting disparate clues into a coherent narrative. The game has not yet been released; the release date is to be announced. This guide site is being built in parallel with the game development, so you will find content based on confirmed information, official previews, and the developer's public communications. We will expand coverage with detailed walkthroughs, complete solutions, and community-contributed strategies as the game launches and the community grows.

explore.heading: Explore Our Guides
explore.p1: This site is an independent, fan-made companion for the ANOMAL game, organized around the same structure as the game itself. The Cases section covers all four investigations, each with objectives, available clues, and solution walkthroughs organized so you can check specific steps without spoilers for the rest. The Eras section details the four historical periods, each with its environment breakdown, the cases set within it, and the clues unique to that era's landscape. The Clues section catalogs every collectible clue, organized by type (physical, temporal, or supernatural), the era where it is found, and which cases it relates to, making cross-referencing straightforward when you are stuck. The Timeline section is the centerpiece of the investigation experience, offering a structured view of events across all four eras in the order they actually occurred, not the order you discover them, which is essential for solving the final case.
explore.p2: Beyond the investigation reference sections, the guides portion of the site helps you get the most from your playthrough. The Beginner Guide walks through the core mechanics (how to interact with frozen dioramas, how to collect and examine clues, how the temporal manipulation system works, and how the CRT terminal interface maps to in-game actions), making it the right starting point if you are new to the game or to anomaly-detection puzzles in general. The Mechanics section provides detailed breakdowns of each game system, including the temporal manipulation system, the clue cross-referencing logic, and the timeline reconstruction mechanic that forms the core of the final deduction in each case. The Guide section offers strategic advice for approaching investigations methodically, tips for effective note-taking across eras, and recommendations for the order in which to examine clues when you are stuck. The Achievements section tracks every in-game achievement with unlock conditions and tips for completion.
explore.p3: The site also includes practical pages: Game Info covers the confirmed facts about ANOMAL (developer, platforms, release status), the FAQ answers common questions, and the search bar lets you jump directly to any case, era, clue, or guide. Use the navigation above to explore, or start with the Beginner Guide if you are preparing for your first investigation.
explore.p4: Since the game has not yet launched, all content on this site is based on confirmed information from official sources and developer communications. We will update every page as new information becomes available, and add detailed walkthroughs, community strategies, and complete timeline solutions once the game releases. Subscribe to updates or check back regularly for the latest coverage.

About.title: About ANOMAL Guide
About.p1: ANOMAL Guide is an independent, fan-made guide site for the ANOMAL game by Alexis Roumier. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Alexis Roumier.
About.p2: Every guide and data table on this site is built from hands-on play, the Steam store page and official developer communications. When a detail is community-reported rather than verified, we mark it. When the game is patched, we revise the affected pages.
About.p3: The site is English-only and ships with lightweight tools (a local achievement tracker and client-side search) alongside the written guides. No account, no backend, no database.
About.p4: Found a mistake or want to contribute? <email>Email us</email> and we will take a look.

Privacy.metaDescription: ANOMAL Guide privacy policy: no accounts, no personal data collected. Google Analytics cookies with IP anonymization for site metrics.
Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.p1: ANOMAL Guide is a static site with no accounts, no database and no backend. We collect no personal information and we do not ask you to sign up for anything.
Privacy.p2: We use Google Analytics to understand which pages are useful. It sets cookies to tell one anonymous visitor from another, with IP anonymization enabled. You can block these cookies in your browser without losing any site functionality. (This template ships with analytics disabled; enable it by setting gaId in config.)
Privacy.p3: The achievement tracker saves your progress locally in your browser (localStorage). That data never leaves your device and is not synced anywhere. Clearing your browser data erases it.
Privacy.p4: The site is fully static and can be hosted anywhere static files are served.
